preconditions.description: The number of vertices in both parts and the number of edges are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n1 and 1 <= v <= n2 for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Every edge connects a valid vertex from the first part to a valid vertex from the second part.
The number of provided edges matches the count m.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly min_degree + 1 lines, one for each k from 0 to min_degree.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line_indices) == line_count for line_count, line_indices in parsed_output)
postconditions.description: For each line, the count of edges matches the number of indices listed.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= idx <= m for idx in indices) and len(set(indices)) == len(indices) for indices in [line[1:] for line in parsed_output])
postconditions.description: All edge indices are within the valid range [1, m] and are distinct within each line.

postconditions.expression: all(all(sum(1 for e_idx in indices if (edges[e_idx-1][0], edges[e_idx-1][1]) == (u, v)) >= k for u, v in all_vertices) for k, indices in enumerate([line[1:] for line in parsed_output]))
postconditions.description: For each k, the selected edges form a k-covering: every vertex in U and V is incident to at least k selected edges.

postconditions.expression: all(len(indices) == min_subset_size(k, edges, n1, n2) for k, indices in enumerate([line[1:] for line in parsed_output]))
postconditions.description: For each k, the number of selected edges is minimal among all possible k-coverings.
